source.title: Noise Is Not the Main Factor Behind the Gap Between SGD and Adam on Transformers, but Sign Descent Might Be
source.authors: Frederik Kunstner; Jacques Chen; J. W. Lavington; M. Schmidt

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training metrics for CIFAR-10 while comparing optimizers and batch sizes, but does not test whether training reaches near-zero classification error under the version’s full set of conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper focuses on training loss and optimizer comparisons. CIFAR-10 training-accuracy results appear in plots, but the text does not describe their values; other reported optimizer results are outside the claim versions.
record.test_reason: ResNet18 trained from random initialization with SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10 directly measures V1's training classification accuracy in Figure 13. The supplied text preserves axes but not readable curves, so the outcome cannot be determined.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: noise is not the main explanation for Adam's advantage on the tested transformer tasks; Adam benefits more from increasing batch size, and sign descent closes much of the full-batch gap. The authors emphasize computational limits, constant step sizes and less clear trends on image tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Compares SGD, Adam, sign descent and normalized gradient updates across batch sizes; it does not evaluate the claim’s random-label or CIFAR-100 conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes optimizer performance; the paper reports different trends for transformer tasks and CIFAR-10/ResNet18.

fits_no_version.finding: On transformer tasks, removing sampling noise does not close the SGD–Adam training-loss gap; sign descent closes much of that gap in full batch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects transformer training progress even without sampling noise, and sign descent shares much of Adam's full-batch advantage.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 training-accuracy results are presented only in plots without textual values. The authors note that their constant step-size and computational limits restrict the runs, and that trends on the image tasks are less clear.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were identified. Optimizer training-loss comparisons and results on MNIST, PTB, WikiText-2 and SQuAD do not measure the behavior named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model-size comparisons, and systematic early-stopping or regularization comparisons. The clean-label CIFAR-10 outcome is measured but unreadable in the supplied text.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies and extra student neurons.
Depth comparisons, plain versus residual networks, and special initialization alternatives.
Initialization comparisons and their effects on signal propagation, training speed or trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to measured stability thresholds, curvature trajectories, catapult recovery and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Controlled comparisons with and without batch normalization or Fixup. The suggested role of batch normalization in CIFAR-10 results is a hypothesis, not a tested comparison.

record.verdict_notes: No directional verdict is justified by unreadable accuracy curves. Axis labels alone do not establish near-zero training error. Hyperparameter-selection values should not become additional outcome rows. Other optimizer comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: The plotted CIFAR-10 training-accuracy results are figure-only and cannot establish whether training classification error is near zero. CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes are not tested.
